docs(webhooks): document Standard Webhooks signing and secret security

Rewrites the signing page around the new scheme: the exact signed
message, the header names, base64 output, the `whsec_` format, and the
fact that the HMAC key is the base64 decoding of the secret rather than
the secret string. Verification leads with an off-the-shelf library,
since interoperability is the point of adopting the standard, and keeps
a hand-rolled example for readers who cannot add a dependency, with the
length check before `timingSafeEqual` and the multi-signature split
spelled out.

The security page gains what the old one promised was coming: secrets
encrypted at rest, what that does and does not protect against, and the
`PAYLOAD_SECRET` dependency. Rotating that key makes every stored secret
unreadable, so the safe procedure is written out in both directions,
along with the recovery path when nobody captured the plaintext first.

The threat model is stated plainly rather than implied. Encryption at
rest defends against database reads. It is not a defence against an
attacker who can write to the database, who can already retarget a
subscription, and ciphertext is not bound to the row it sits in.
Overstating this would be worse than saying nothing.

Also documents the adoption utility for pre-encryption subscriptions and
notes that receivers must change regardless, since the format, headers,
and key derivation all moved.

The form-builder comment distinguishing its own signing scheme referred
to a header this release deletes, so it now names the current one.

feat(webhooks): add an adoption path for pre-encryption secrets

Subscriptions written before secrets were encrypted still hold plaintext.
`encryptExistingSecrets(payload)` normalizes each one to `whsec_<base64>`
and encrypts it in place, skipping rows that already hold ciphertext so
the run is idempotent and safe to repeat. A dry run reports without
writing.

Normalizing does not invent a new secret. A legacy 48-character hex
secret is already valid base64, so it keeps its characters and gains the
`whsec_` prefix: the value an operator holds still works when handed to
a Standard Webhooks verifier in prefixed form. Receivers must be updated
regardless, because the signature scheme itself changed.

A secret that cannot be normalized is reported with its row id rather
than rewritten, since guessing would silently break signing. Those need
a rotation.

Reading the stored value needs a third reveal flag: `forSigning` cannot
serve it, because a legacy unprefixed secret fails the decrypt path's
`whsec_` check and reads back as null. Like the other flags it lives in
`req.context`, which no REST or GraphQL caller can set.

test(webhooks): verify deliveries against the reference implementation

Adds `standardwebhooks` as a dev dependency and asserts that a delivery
produced by the plugin is accepted by the library customers are expected
to verify with, rather than by a local helper that reimplements our own
algorithm and would agree with any mistake we made.

This is what pins the secret-to-key derivation. The reference verifier
strips `whsec_` and base64-decodes the remainder into the HMAC key, so
keying with the undecoded ASCII would pass a self-consistent test suite
and fail every real receiver. Negative cases (tampered body, unrelated
secret, swapped delivery id) confirm the verifier rejects, so a passing
result means something.

Rotation is covered from the receiving side too: verifiers holding
either secret accept during the grace period, and the retired one stops
verifying after it lapses.

The documented receiver example is kept here in behaviour so a change to
the published snippet that breaks verification fails the suite. Its
timestamp tolerance is exercised on both sides of the boundary, with
offsets measured from the delivery's own timestamp so the margin under
test does not shrink on a loaded run.

webhooks: support secret rotation

A subscription's signing secret could only be replaced by deleting and
recreating the subscription. It can now be rotated in place, generated
or customer-supplied, through a `POST /:id/rotate-secret` endpoint that
mirrors the existing redeliver endpoint, plus a doc-view button that
mirrors RedeliverButton. The new secret is returned exactly once, the
same reveal contract as create.

The outgoing secret keeps signing for `secretRotation.graceSeconds`
(default 24h, per-call override), so deliveries carry a signature from
both secrets and receivers can switch over without dropping events.
Standard Webhooks already specifies space-separated signatures for
exactly this, so the multi-signature header needs nothing new on the
receiving side.

Expiry is evaluated at resolve time from the stored timestamp rather
than by a scheduled job. The timestamp is the entire state, so the
window stays correct across restarts, and the old secret stops signing
the moment it lapses instead of whenever a job next happens to run.

Both secrets are stored encrypted through the same beforeChange path,
and both read back masked.

webhooks: encrypt subscription secrets at rest

Signing secrets were stored as plaintext, so database access was secret
access. They now go through Payload's own `encrypt`/`decrypt` in the
subscriptions `beforeChange`, before the value reaches the database.

Stored ciphertext carries a `whenc1_` tag. Payload's cipher is
aes-256-ctr, whose output is unauthenticated and indistinguishable from
arbitrary text, and whose `decrypt` returns garbage rather than throwing
on a wrong key. Trial decryption therefore cannot answer "is this
already encrypted?", so the tag is what makes the hook idempotent and
keeps an update from encrypting an already-encrypted secret again.

Reveal behaviour is unchanged from the customer's side. The create
response still shows the plaintext exactly once, now served from a
request-scoped stash because the response reads back ciphertext.
`forSigning` decrypts for internal delivery reads. Every other read
still sees the mask.

Two failure modes are handled explicitly: a decrypt that does not yield
a well-formed `whsec_` secret returns null and logs, so a rotated
PAYLOAD_SECRET stops signing rather than signing with a garbage key; and
a masked value written back on update is dropped instead of persisting
the placeholder as the signing key.

The integration test reads the stored document straight from the mongo
driver, since an API response cannot prove encryption at rest when the
mask hook shapes it either way.

webhooks: reserve the headers the delivery pipeline owns

A subscription's custom headers are spread over the generated ones, so a
header named `webhook-signature` replaced the real signature and one
named `webhook-id` changed the value the MAC was computed over. Either
made every delivery unverifiable, and the signature case let a
subscription author choose the value receivers check.

`withoutReservedHeaders` now filters `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`,
`webhook-signature`, and `X-Webhook-Event` out of custom headers before
the spread, matching case-insensitively because HTTP header names are.

Filtering alone would drop the header silently, so both sources reject
it up front instead: a field `validate` on the headers array for
admin-managed subscriptions, and a config-build assertion for code
subscriptions.

webhooks: align signing with Standard Webhooks

Signatures are now HMAC-SHA256 over `${id}.${timestamp}.${body}`, base64
encoded, keyed by the base64-decoded secret, and carried as
`webhook-signature: v1,<sig>` alongside `webhook-id` and
`webhook-timestamp`. `X-Webhook-Event` is retained; the pre-standard
`X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature` headers
are gone.

The key is the base64 decoding of the secret after its `whsec_` prefix,
matching what the reference `standardwebhooks` verifier does. Keying the
HMAC with the undecoded ASCII would produce signatures no off-the-shelf
Standard Webhooks library accepts.

Secrets are generated as `whsec_<base64>` over 32 random bytes.
Customer-supplied secrets are normalized to exactly one prefix and
validated as base64 carrying at least 16 bytes, so a doubly-prefixed or
non-base64 value can never reach the HMAC. Malformed input fails with a
400 on create and at config build for code subscriptions, where a bad
secret would otherwise surface only as receivers rejecting every
delivery.

A resolved subscription now carries `secrets: string[]` rather than one
optional secret, which is what multi-signature rotation will fill in.

dividers and no subpixel hairline, and the hover/focus sync targets a
single element. Buttons become borderless react-select-style indicators,
muted until hovered. Glyphs are redrawn centered on the icon canvas
(dropping a leftover translate that shifted them right).

* fix(fields): cluster border mirrors input state only, no junction edge

Remove the input's right border in attached rows instead of painting
over it: with the cluster carrying no left border either, no vertical
edge exists at the junction to divide, misalign, or leak a hairline.
The cluster stretches to the input's height rather than declaring one.

Border sync now reads exactly the input's own states via :has(): hover
(including label-propagated hover) lights both to elevation-250, focus
to elevation-400, and hovering an action animates only the icon, never
the control border.

* fix(fields): one border for the whole attached control

Move the single border, radius, background, shadow, and transition onto
the row itself and strip the native input of all chrome: input text and
action icons now sit inside literally one border, so no combination of
states (the focused+hovered mismatch included) can ever render them
differently. Row states replicate formInput's precedence via :where
(hover 250 with deepened shadow, focus 400 declared later so it wins),
driven by the input's own :hover (label propagation included) and
:focus-within; hovering an action still only animates the icon. Error
styling mirrors Payload's light/darkInputError onto the row, and the
write-only editor now sets the error class like the masked input does.

Neighbouring actions halve their facing paddings so icons sit close
while the cluster stays fully clickable edge to edge.

* fix(fields): concealed values render as text, save ends the reveal window

A stored value's concealed face (hint or dots) is real data, not a
prompt, so it now renders in the input's text color everywhere: the
write-only placeholder gains a --set modifier, and the masked value
dots, textarea, and structural faces move from elevation-500 to 800.
A true placeholder (unset field) keeps formInput's native muted style.

The reveal-once window now closes on save instead of page leave: both
write-only variants subscribe to useDocumentEvents and drop the staged
plaintext the moment the edit view reports a successful save (failed
validation fires no event, so typed input survives it). Payload's
post-save form-state refresh already carries the new set/hint siblings,
so the concealed face shows the rotated hint immediately.

* feat(fields): explicit intent semantics for the write-only editor

Extract the staged-intent transitions into a pure, exhaustively tested
state machine (writeOnlyIntent). Three unmistakable staged states:
concealed face (text-colored hint/dots) keeps, visible plaintext
replaces, and a muted 'Will be removed on save' notice with an undo
arrow clears. Erasing staged text now returns to the state the user was
in when they started typing, so a clear followed by a half-typed
replacement is never silently cancelled; type-then-erase-then-save on a
populated field provably keeps the stored value. Staged text trims
surrounding whitespace on blur, so a pasted trailing newline never
seals into a credential nobody can read back to debug.

Server guard: a write-only empty-string write clears like null instead
of sealing '', which would read as set while holding nothing. Covered
by hook unit tests and an int case; other encrypted fields keep sealing
'' unchanged.

* fix(fields): save-conceal must not re-dirty the form

Payload's useField setValue marks the whole form modified unless passed
disableModifyingForm, so the write-only save-conceal effect (which folds
the field back to its concealed face after a successful save) was
re-dirtying the form Payload had just marked clean: every save of a
write-only field resurrected the leave-without-saving warning on the
next navigation. Both variants now pass disableModifyingForm for that
housekeeping write; user-initiated writes (type, clear, undo, generate,
trim) still dirty the form as they should. Cancelling an untouched
structural editor no longer dirties the form either.

Audited every setValue call site in the plugin: all remaining ones are
direct user interactions.

* fix(fields): review round: set-indicator recursion, cell a11y, docs

makeSetIndicatorHook now recurses presence checks, so a locale map of
arrays ({ en: [] }, { en: [null] }) reads as unset instead of set. The
unset list cell's em-dash glyph gains an accessible 'Not set' label
(secretNotSet key, en+de). Docs example imports GlobalConfig so it
typechecks when copied, and the hasMany handle wording says decrypt()
resolves an array. Worktree-dev skill adds docker ps to the finishing
audit. run.ts worktree detection accepts Windows separators, and the
port comment states allocation honestly: stable and best-effort unique,
Next reports the actual port on a rare collision, PORT overrides.

* fix(fields): generator charset hardening, hint gap-glyph guard

normalizeGenerate now dedupes the charset into a code-point array and
rejects more than 256 distinct characters: beyond that, byte-based
rejection sampling has a zero acceptance window and the generator loop
never terminates. Sampling from the array keeps the distribution
uniform over distinct symbols and never splits an astral character
into surrogate halves. generate.length docs now say rejected, not
clamped, matching behavior.

makeHint stores no hint when an exposed end contains the mask glyph
(U+00B7): a dot in the exposed text would blur where the concealed
span starts. Real credentials never carry it, so this only closes the
ambiguity. The write-only input also gains min-width: 0 so it can
shrink instead of pushing attached actions out of narrow containers.

fix(folder-picker): stop the dev database and the seed from wedging

An `exit` listener cannot await anything, so stopping the in-memory replica set from one

stop and re-raise, and the `exit` listener is gone.

The dev seed memoised the promise it returned, including a rejected one, so a single

fix(folder-picker): report a refused move or delete instead of reloading

fetch rejects only on a network failure, so a 401, 403 or 500 arrived as an ordinary
response and was never inspected. Both handlers went straight on to clear the selection
and reload, presenting a refusal as a success: the same rows back, no message, and the
user believing the move or the delete had happened.

Both check the response now and surface the server's own message as a toast. Deleting
stops at the first refusal rather than working through the rest, since whatever denied
one will deny the others, while the view is still refreshed for anything already gone.

fix(folder-picker): filter the grid, keep the search box, survive a failed load

Four things in the folder view, all found by review.

**The grid ignored the search.** The server builds its grid with the items baked in and
its table with none, so the table reads the provider and the grid cannot. Narrowing the
provider therefore filtered one view and not the other: searching in grid mode left the
count and the cards disagreeing, and could draw the empty state over a full grid. The grid
is rebuilt here from the same filtered arrays, with the card grid Payload builds it from,
and its group headings come from the collection labels rather than the server's hard-coded
English.

**The search box emptied itself.** It sat inside the folder provider, which is rebuilt
whenever the view or the folder changes, and held the typed text in its own state. Toggling
the view or opening a folder wiped the box while the term it had already reported went on
filtering the results. The text and its debounce moved out to the view that owns those
results, and the input is controlled.

**Loading raced with itself and could not fail.** Breadcrumbs, cards, the sort pill, the
toggle and the mount effect all load, and each load writes six pieces of state, so a slow
early request resolving after a fast later one put one folder's contents under another
folder's breadcrumb. Responses now check they are still the one being awaited. A rejection
had no handler at all and every call site fires and forgets, so a failed first load left
the drawer under its loading overlay for good; it now reports the error and offers a retry.

**The view toggles had no accessible name.** Both are icon only, so they announced as two
unlabelled buttons with no way to tell them apart. They carry an aria-label and aria-pressed
now. Payload's own toggles have neither, so the names are new plugin keys, as are the sort
menu group labels, which were hard-coded English in a component where everything else was
translated. The search input also drops its id, since Payload's own hard-codes the same one
and two of those in a document break every association pointing at it.

fix(folder-picker): do not offer to edit a folder when a file is selected

The edit action feeds its target's id to a drawer keyed to the folder collection, and the
target could be any selected item. Selecting a file and choosing edit therefore looked up
a file id among folders and sent the admin to /admin/collections/<folders>?notFound=<id>.

A document is no longer a target for it. Payload's own selection bar hides the action in
exactly this case, leaving the bulk document actions to handle a document selection.
Editing the folder in view, and editing a selected folder, are untouched.

fix(folder-picker): pin the dragged card to the cursor

dnd-kit preserves the grab point, so a card taken by its lower edge followed the cursor
from that edge and sat over whatever was being dragged onto. The card now pins its top
left just below and right of the cursor however it was picked up, which is what the
folder view does on the route.

Payload applies a modifier for this on its own overlay but exports neither it nor the
overlay, so it is reproduced beside the card that was already reproduced. The coordinate
read it depends on lives in @dnd-kit/utilities, which reaches this package only through
@dnd-kit/core and would have to become a second peer dependency; two numbers off an
event are not worth that.

feat(fields): layered icon libraries with library-supplied labels (#91)

* fix(fields): honour icon fallback when a client icon fails to resolve

createIcon rendered nothing when loadIcon resolved null, while createRscIcon returned the
caller's fallback. The docs document the RSC behaviour as the contract, so the client was
the side that was wrong.

The lazy component is cached module-wide on library:name, so it cannot close over any one
caller's fallback prop. A FallbackContext carries it instead, with the provider rendered
only when a fallback is present, leaving the common decorative call byte-identical.

createRscIcon also gains the per-value resolution cache it never had. A static loadIcon
rides the module cache, but an HTTP-backed one paid one fetch per render. Rejections evict,
matching the manifest cache, so a transient failure cannot poison an icon for the process
lifetime.

* feat(fields): let an icon library supply a human-readable label

IconMeta gains an optional label. Without one the name is sentence-cased exactly as
before, so every existing manifest and both bundled libraries are unaffected. It is a
StaticLabel, matching IconAdapter.label, so a per-locale label resolves for free.

Names that are codes rather than words could not produce a correct label: HUN read as
Hun. That fed the drawer tooltip and, more importantly, the cell aria-label, so a screen
reader browsing a country library announced 215 three-letter codes.

The accessible name and the tooltip now differ on purpose. The accessible name carries
the label alone. The tooltip carries the raw name alongside it, because that is the only
surface where an editor can discover "Hungary" stores as HUN, which they need to write
frontend code against the value.

The field trigger and list cell hold only a stored value, so IconAdapter gains an
optional resolveMeta: one exact lookup serving both existence and label. It defaults to
the manifest index, now keyed by name rather than a bare name set. A library whose
contents change at runtime supplies its own and stays correct where a cached snapshot
cannot.

The grid cell moves out of the drawer into IconGridCell, so the accessible name has a
rendering assertion rather than a snapshot. A snapshot would have passed throughout this
defect's life.

* feat(fields): accept non-kebab icon names in manifest codegen

generateIconManifest required kebab-case, which rejected a library keyed by code and
forced its author to hand-write an emitter. Kebab-case was never the real constraint,
only the shape the two bundled libraries happened to have. It is the same wrong
assumption as deriving a display label from the name.

The actual constraint is narrower: a name must be non-empty and free of whitespace,
control characters, ":" (which separates library from name in a stored value), and the
quote and backslash that would escape the emitted key in imports.ts. Everything else is
legitimate, including uppercase and non-latin scripts.

That quote and backslash guard also moves into emitImportsModule itself. The name is
interpolated bare as a map key there, and the kebab regex had been covering that by
accident; the emitter is exported and callable directly, so it now stands on its own.

Names differing only by case are rejected, because drawer search normalises case and an
editor cannot tell them apart. This is a new restriction on existing third-party
manifests. Radix and tabler regenerate byte-identically.

* test(fields): pin how the bundled icon libraries render

Characterization net for lucide, radix and tabler, so the layer and render-strategy work
cannot move them without saying so.

A sha256 over every glyph in a library covers ground no hand-written sample could: 1500
lucide and 4900 tabler glyphs, each rendered through DrawerGlyph. Exact markup assertions
sit beside the hashes so a failure names what broke rather than only that something did.

The hashes were taken from a tree where client/DrawerGlyph.tsx and all of adapters/ are
byte-identical to main, so they pin shipped output rather than this branch's.

Also asserts no bundled manifest carries a per-icon label, and that every icon in all
three libraries still derives the label it always did. If a bundled manifest ever gained
one, every label in that library would change at once.

* feat(fields): compose icon libraries from ordered layers

An adapter may now declare layers: ordered sources under one slug, later winning by name
and free to add names the base lacks. That is what a static package plus runtime-supplied
overrides needs, and a helper that merged sources into one adapter could not express it,
because the drawer has to paint different layers with different strategies in one grid.

Entirely additive. An adapter with no layers keeps every existing path untouched, and the
characterization net over lucide, radix and tabler still passes unchanged.

Manifest listings cache per layer to a declared policy, defaulting to 'forever', which is
how a static build artifact has always been cached. Validation deliberately does not read
that cache: it goes through resolveMeta, so an icon added at runtime is valid immediately
even while the listing is stale.

The cache key includes a layer-supplied cacheKey. Slug and layer id are identical across
tenants by construction, so without it a scoped layer would serve one tenant's library to
another. A test covers exactly that.

resolveMetaMany batches lookups issued in one microtask. The window is a microtask rather
than a request because the surface with the most to gain has no request to key on: Payload
renders list cells with payload and i18n only. Eight icon fields on one document, or fifty
list rows, collapse to one call.

Duplicate layer ids are rejected at registration, since they key the cache, and each
layer's render path is registered in admin.dependencies or generate:importmap would drop it.

* feat(fields): let an icon layer declare how its glyphs render

DrawerGlyph stops hardcoding lucide's canvas and takes it from the layer, and IconNode
gains an optional third element for children. A filled 15x15 set is now as renderable as
a 24x24 stroked one, and arbitrary SVG needing g or defs is expressible where a flat node
list could not say it.

Defaults are exactly the constants the drawer hardcoded before, so a library declaring no
canvas is untouched. The characterization hashes over all 1500 lucide and 4900 tabler
glyphs are unchanged, which is the proof rather than the claim.

Adds the svg strategy's sprite builder: bulk SVG is parsed and sanitised once into one
symbol document, and each cell then renders use href. No per-icon request, and no reparse
per cell.

Sanitising uses DOMPurify rather than an allowlist written here. The trust level is lower
than it looks: on a multi-tenant install an upload layer's SVGs are written by per-tenant
editors, customers rather than operators, and this markup renders inline into the shared
admin. Test vectors cover script, event handlers, foreignObject, javascript: and data:
URIs, cross-document use, and style carrying import.

ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP turned out to be the wrong knob, since DOMPurify validates every
attribute against it and restricting it to fragments also stripped d and viewBox. A hook
on a module-private instance narrows the rule to href and xlink:href instead, so internal
defs-and-use references keep working and no host app's own DOMPurify is affected.

* feat(fields): resolve frontend icons through renderer layers

IconRendererAdapter gains optional layers, walked newest first, so an override wins and an
older layer still serves names the newer one lacks. That is the shape a static package
plus runtime overrides needs on the frontend, which is where the first consumer resolves
theirs.

Both factories go through one resolver, so the client and server paths cannot drift on
precedence the way they had drifted on fallback.

Additive: a renderer with no layers keeps using loadIcon, which is every renderer written
before this. Kept separate from the admin IconAdapter deliberately, since merging them
would drag manifest and drawer code into a frontend bundle.

The RSC resolution cache now keys layered results too, so a repeated value asks each layer
once rather than per render.

* perf(fields): render radix icons from bulk node data

Radix sat on the drawer's per-icon path for one reason: it ships React components rather
than raw SVG, so there was no node-data to render in bulk, and its 15x15 filled canvas
would have rendered stroked under the hardcoded outline convention. Both are now
addressable, so it can join lucide and tabler.

Node-data comes from rendering each component once at generation time and parsing the
result. That extraction lives in this repo's scripts rather than the published codegen,
deliberately: it needs a DOM, and jsdom has no business becoming a runtime dependency of
@10x-media/fields/icon/codegen for consumers who only generate their own libraries. The
public 'radix' source still emits manifest and imports exactly as before.

IconAdapter gains an optional canvas for its Nodes glyphs, defaulting to the outline
convention, so every library that shipped without one is unaffected. Radix declares its own.

Adds a golden hash over all 318 radix glyphs plus explicit fill and viewBox assertions, so
the set cannot drift silently.

Also fixes a missing barrel export found while verifying this: the adapter declared
RadixAdapterNodes but exports/icon-adapters/radix.ts never exported it. getFromImportMap
runs with silent:true by design, so the drawer degraded quietly to the per-icon path and
nothing looked wrong. A new test walks every bundled adapter's declared component paths and
asserts the named subpath actually exports them; reverting the fix makes it fail.

* test(fields): close the import-map wiring loop for bundled adapters

Extends the export gate to the hop that actually fails silently: building a payload-shaped
import map from the real barrels and asserting getFromImportMap resolves every component
path each bundled adapter declares.

The three links are now covered end to end. The adapter names a path, the barrel exports
it, and the map resolves it. A break in any one degraded quietly to the per-icon path
before, because getFromImportMap runs with silent:true by design.

* feat(fields): serve dynamic icon manifests and add an upload-collection layer

A library whose data lives on the server is now written once, server-side, with req in
hand. The plugin registers the endpoint the drawer reads it through, so no consumer has to
hand-roll one and invent their own auth and caching story.

The endpoint is registered only when a server layer exists, so a config without one is
untouched. It requires an authenticated user, and gates on the same availability rule as
every other surface including the alwaysAvailable union, or a globally offered library
would be pickable in the field and unreachable here. A failing layer answers 500 rather
than an empty library, since "no icons found" would read to an editor as an empty library
rather than a fault. Nothing is browser-cacheable, because the listing can change between
requests.

uploadIconLayer points at an upload collection so editors can add icons without a deploy.
It is the proof the layer contract holds: anything a real upload-backed library needs that
only this file can express would be a gap in the contract.

It defaults to the url strategy, which renders through an img and cannot execute script.
svg inlines editor-written markup into the shared admin, where on a multi-tenant install
the uploader is a customer rather than an operator, so that is opt-in.

Validation never reads the cached listing: resolveMeta issues one exact query and
resolveMetaMany batches a tick's lookups into a single in-clause. An icon uploaded a moment
ago is therefore valid immediately on every instance, which is the freshness gap that
motivated layers.

* docs(fields): document layered icon libraries and label support

New layers page covering ordered sources, why listing and lookup are separate jobs, cache
policy and the cacheKey requirement for scoped layers, batched lookups, the four render
strategies, the manifest endpoint, and the trust trade-off between the url and svg
strategies for uploaded icons.

Updates adapters with the optional icon label, resolveMeta, and the deliberate split
between the accessible name and the tooltip; codegen with the real name rules; and
frontend rendering with renderer layers and the now-true fallback contract.

Changeset is a minor, and calls out the case-insensitive duplicate check as a possible
breaking change for a hand-written third-party manifest.

* fix(fields): widen upload-layer documents through unknown

The dev app and every real consumer generate payload types, which makes CollectionSlug a
concrete union and DataFromCollectionSlug a union of generated document types. Those have
no index signature, so asserting the find result straight to Record<string, unknown> is
rejected there.

It passed in the package's own typecheck because CollectionSlug is unconstrained without
generated types, so the failure only appeared once CI typechecked the dev app. Mapping each
document through an unknown-taking helper keeps it one legal assertion rather than a double
cast.

* feat(fields): add encryptedField factory with validate-preserving hooks

Wrap 12 Payload field types in AES-256-GCM at rest. The factory returns a
text-backed stored field (plus a hidden ${name}_bidx sibling when queryable)
whose beforeChange hook seals and afterRead hook unseals; the seal hook runs
the effective plaintext validator itself and the composed validate skips
sealed values, since Payload runs field beforeChange hooks before validate.

typescriptSchema keeps each source type's generated shape; hooks respect the
tenxFieldsEncrypted context mode (raw/rotate/decrypt) and derive keys from
config.secret. AAD is built through buildAad so a dotted slug/locale fails
closed. queryable is gated to scalar text/email/number (blind index needs a
scalar) and rejects hasMany; unique moves onto the bidx sibling.

Adds @types/json-schema for the typescriptSchema typing.

* fix(fields): decouple encrypted blind-index key from the active data key

Deriving the blind-index HMAC key from the active data key meant rotating that
key silently changed the index key, so every previously written bidx stopped
matching and equality queries missed all un-rotated rows. Derive the index key
from a stable root instead: an optional dedicated KeysConfig.indexKey, else the
Payload secret. Data-key rotation now re-seals ciphertext while the blind index
stays byte-identical, so queries keep matching. indexKey material is length-
validated like data keys.

* fix(fields): validate full wire structure in isSealed

isSealed only checked the prefix and dot count, so a free-text secret literally
shaped 'pfe1.a.b.c.d' passed as sealed and skipped its plaintext validation.
Validate the whole wire structure (base64url charset, 12-byte IV, 16-byte tag,
non-empty ciphertext) via parseWire in wire.ts and a crypto-free structural
replica in validators.ts (which runs in Payload's validate pass and must not
import node:crypto).

* fix(fields): strip defaultValue and inert type props from encrypted stored field

A static defaultValue on the stored text field emits a PLAINTEXT column default
in drizzle, so an INSERT that omits the column writes plaintext at rest. Strip
it. Also strip source-type-only constraints (options, min, max, minLength,
maxLength) that are inert on a text column; the effective validator already
enforces them on plaintext.

* test(fields): assert blind index depends on index-key material, not the data key

Follow-up to the index-key decoupling: the key-dependence assertion built a
second ring from different data-key material, which now shares the secret-derived
index key. Use distinct indexKey material to exercise a distinct blind index.

* fix(fields): seal per item, validate plaintext in the native validate pass

H1 (data corruption): the hasMany seal path used an all-or-nothing already-sealed
guard, so a mixed [sealed, plaintext] array fell through to map(seal) and wrapped
the already-sealed items in a second GCM layer. Seal per item instead, passing
each already-sealed item through byte-identical.

M1/M2 (drafts + error aggregation): the seal hook validated plaintext and threw
ValidationError mid-traversal, which ignored skipValidation (drafts/autosave),
hid other fields' errors, used a bare field name for the path, and had no req.t.
Payload runs field beforeChange hooks before validate, so instead the hook now
stashes the pre-seal plaintext on req.context and the composed validate reads it
back and validates the plaintext in Payload's native validate pass, which honors
skipValidation and aggregates errors with the right path and req.t.

M3 (locale=all writes): a locale=all write handed the hook a { [locale]: value }
map, which was sealed as one blob under the default-locale AAD and could not be
opened by afterRead's per-locale unseal. Seal each locale under its own locale
AAD; validation and blind-index maintenance for bulk all-locales writes are
deferred to per-locale writes (Batch E int coverage).

L5: decrypt context mode now also clears the ${name}_bidx sibling.

* fix(fields): key encrypted plaintext stash by sealed value to fix bulk-write validation race

The M2 plaintext stash keyed by field path, but req.context is shared across the
documents of a bulk/concurrent write (payload.update({ where, data }) runs
docs.map + Promise.all with one req). Every concurrent document of the same field
wrote and read the SAME stash slot (path 'ssn' is identical for all), and
takePlaintext deletes on first read, so some documents' validate saw no stash and
skipped (bypass) while others validated another document's plaintext. Silent
validation-integrity hole under concurrency, not a plaintext leak.

Key the stash by the SEALED VALUE the hook just produced instead: the seal hook
mints a fresh IV per write, so the ciphertext is unique per document, and Payload
hands the composed validate exactly that sealed value. Single value keys by the
sealed string; hasMany keys by the joined sealed items. Collision-free across
documents, requests, and paths, preserving all four write-path semantics
(direct-API, admin form state, null/required, resubmitted-sealed).

Adds a concurrency test (5 single-value + 4 hasMany documents through the real
seal hook + composed validate sharing one req.context) asserting every document
validates its OWN value.

explicit (or default) UTC reporting timezone silently produced project-local
days on non-UTC projects. The resolved zone is now passed unconditionally.

fix(analytics): scope widget metric picker to the selected data source

became an SVG triangle in line with Payload's icon components, and a zero
baseline renders the localized direction word instead of a bare dash.

A previous window derived from raw instants started mid-day, so the native
adapter's period filter silently dropped the window's first daily rollup and
biased every delta upward. The window now spans whole reporting-timezone days

instead of comparing against a pre-1970 window, and the trend series no longer
coerces a missing previous total to 0. Both engine reads run in parallel, and
widgets.comparison: false skips the previous-window read entirely.

feat: add @10x-media/analytics plugin (#15)

Adds `@10x-media/analytics`, an adapter-based analytics plugin for Payload v3.

## What it does

- **Unified adapter contract** with capability gating: third-party providers and a first-party native engine are all adapters; admin surfaces render only what the active adapter supports and auto-disable otherwise.
- **Adapters**: native (Payload-backed), GA4, Plausible, Umami, PostHog, each code-split into its own subpath so a site bundles only what it uses.
- **Native engine**: cookieless ingestion, append-only events plus pre-aggregated rollups (atomic, cross-DB), pluggable geo resolution, retention pruning, and a daily time-series read path.
- **Surfacing**: on-demand reads cached in `payload.kv` (coalescing, bounded queue, backoff), per-kind TTLs, day-snapped cache keys, and a provider look-back clamp.
- **Per-document display fields**: portable, capability-gated, read-only stat and tab field factories (server components, `/rsc` subpath); nothing is injected automatically.
- **Dashboard widgets** (Payload's modular dashboard): metric, trend (gradient area chart), four breakdowns (pages/sources/devices/countries), a live "active now" realtime widget, custom date ranges, and a public `widgets.register` extension API.
- **Background tiers**, both opt-in and off by default: a scheduled cache-warm job, and a sync tier that periodically ETLs each provider's daily metrics into a queryable `analytics-daily` collection.

Cross-DB (Mongo and Postgres) verified via the test matrix. First beta release: `0.1.0-beta.0`.

fix(test-harness): eliminate pg pool teardown race on container stop

Drizzle's destroy() clears its schema/drizzle handles but never ends the
node-postgres pool, so after payload.destroy() the pool's idle connections
stay open. The Postgres testcontainer is then SIGKILLed (timeout: 0), which
terminates those connections and emits FATAL 57P01 errors. node-postgres
re-emits idle-client failures on the pool's `error` event, and with no
listener they surfaced as unhandled rejections (vitest "Errors: N"): 36 in
@10x-media/jobs, 1 in @10x-media/webhooks.

Attach a pool `error` handler at teardown so these expected container-stop
errors are handled rather than unhandled. Draining instead (await pool.end())
was tried and rejected: it hangs on suites that hold a checked-out client at
teardown (jobs reliability/heartbeat/worker tests), timing out the afterAll
hook. Mongo tiers are unaffected (mongoose's db exposes no `.pool`).

Verified: jobs + webhooks test:matrix now report 0 unhandled errors, 0 hook
timeouts, all tests passing on both Mongo and Postgres.
